memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Lot went outside to meet them and shut the door behind him and said, "No, my friends. Don't do this wicked thing. Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you, and you can do what you like with them. But don't do anything to these men, for they have come under the protection of my roof." - Gen 19:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most troubling verses in Genesis, and we must not soften it. Lot rightly refuses to hand over his guests - but then, appallingly, he offers his own daughters to the mob. What are we to make of this? Scripture reports it without approving it. This was a grievous, sinful act - no father should ever offer his children to be harmed, and nothing here is held up as a model.

What we see is the tragic wreckage of a compromised life. Years of living in Sodom had twisted even Lot's moral instincts. He was right to protect his guests, yet so shaped by that corrupt culture that he was willing to sacrifice his own daughters. Compromise does not stay contained; it distorts our thinking until we can defend the indefensible.

This is a sobering warning about the cost of a compromised life. Lot was a believer, yet dwelling in Sodom had deformed his judgement. Where we choose to live, what we soak our minds in, the culture we absorb - these shape us more than we know, often for the worse.

Let this drive us not to condemnation of Lot but to humble self-examination. How has the world around us bent our thinking? Only Christ can straighten what sin has twisted. We need our minds constantly renewed by God's Word, lest we too "conform to the pattern of this world" (Rom 12:2) until we can no longer see clearly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- How might the culture around you be quietly distorting your thinking?
- Where do you need your mind renewed by God's Word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, this scene warns me how compromise distorts the heart. Guard my mind from being bent by the world around me. Renew my thinking by Your Word, that I may see clearly and live rightly.
Amen.
